Preface
 
CCF Computility is established as a premier platform for industry professionals, academic scholars, and re-
searchers to exchange innovative ideas, methodologies, and technological advancements in the field of distribut-
ed computing systems. Formerly known as the CCF (China Computer Federation) Annual Conference on Dis-
tributed and Parallel Computing Systems (CCF DPCS), CCF Computility has evolved to better address the
rapidly growing importance of computility (算力)—a new dimension of productive capacity that is driving trans-
formative development across multiple sectors.
In recent years, the research and development of networked computing infrastructure, collectively referred to
as computility (算力网), has become a central topic across industry, academia, and research communities. To
more effectively align with academic trends and research frontiers, the CCF Technical Committee on Distribut-
ed Computing and Systems has renamed CCF DPCS to CCF Computility.
The inaugural CCF Computility conference was held from July 26 to 28, 2024, in Changchun, with Jilin Uni-
versity serving as the primary host. Centered around the theme “The Computility (算力网): Distributed Sys-
tems Under New Quality Productivity”, the conference explored a diverse range of topics within distributed sys-
tems. These included the multifaceted nature of computility, advancements in emerging computer networks, dis-
tributed storage infrastructures, system software, security challenges in computility, key applications, and the
latest developments in cloud and edge computing. CCF Computility 2024 attracted significant attention from
both academia and industry, receiving 96 paper submissions, 39 of which were in English.
From these English submissions, four outstanding papers have been selected for inclusion in this special sec-
tion. The selected papers encompass a wide spectrum of topics, such as carbon-aware energy cost optimization
for geo-distributed data centers, distributed training methods for edge clusters, joint routing and scheduling for
mixed flows in time-sensitive networks, and fault tolerance mechanisms in high-performance computing systems.
In  addition,  this  special  section  features  two  invited  papers  on  distributed  architectures  for  computility  and
trusted multi-cloud authentication.
We hope that readers will find this special section both informative and inspiring. We extend our sincere
gratitude to all the authors and reviewers for their invaluable contributions.
Guest Editors

Xiao-Wei Li is a professor at the Institute of Computing Technology (ICT), Chinese Academy of
Sciences (CAS), Beijing. He received his B.Eng. and M.Eng. degrees in computer science from Hefei
University of Technology, Hefei, in 1985 and 1988, respectively, and his Ph.D. degree in computer
science from ICT, CAS, Beijing, in 1991. His research interests encompass VLSI testing, fault-toler-
ant design, and hardware security. Dr. Li has co-authored six books and published over 380 papers
in leading academic journals and international conferences. He is a recipient of the National Techno-
logical Invention Award (2012) and the National Science and Technology Progress Award (2015).
Dr. Li currently serves as Vice-Chair of the IEEE Computer Society Test Technology Technical Council and is a Fel-
low of CCF.
